model_annotation: This line and bar chart illustrates the monthly trends of German exports, imports, and the trade balance (Saldo) from 2020 through 2023, with values expressed in billions of US dollars. The horizontal x-axis represents time, spanning from early 2020 to late 2023, marked annually with intermediate tick marks for each month. The vertical y-axis on the left (linke Skala) measures export and import values, ranging from 0 to 400 billion USD, with major gridlines every 50 billion. The vertical y-axis on the right (rechte Skala) measures the trade balance, ranging from -200 to 400 billion USD, with major gridlines every 100 billion. The blue solid line represents imports, starting near 200 billion USD in early 2020, dipping slightly before rising steadily to approximately 350 billion USD by late 2023. The purple solid line represents exports, beginning around 135 billion USD in early 2020, declining briefly, then gradually increasing to roughly 180 billion USD by the end of the period. The light blue vertical bars indicate the monthly trade balance (Saldo), calculated as exports minus imports; they start near +15 billion USD in early 2020, dip into negative territory (deficit) in mid-2020, recover to small surpluses through 2021–2022, and then decline sharply into a large deficit of approximately -150 billion USD by late 2023.
